newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa pauses, may rise in PM.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa pauses, may rise in PM.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures were just touch firmer by Thursday midsession after an early advance failed to trigger buy-stops but traders said the upside move could resume in the afternoon.
"The market advanced early to attract some stops. It pulled back slightly as nothing appeared on the upside," said one trader.
Benchmark September's high-point was 1,145 stg a tonne. It then retreated to a low of 1,135 before finishing the morning trade three stg higher at 1,140.
December was jut one stg up at 1,141.
Technically, while the 1,100 stg level basis September remained intact, there was also scope for the market to blip higher to 1,172, analysts said.
Traders called the New York market to open $5-$10 higher and this could encourage an upward swing in London.
The U.S. futures saw some good industry-oriented buying on Wednesday. But the market still finished lower in what traders described as a small setback.
"The extent and vigour of the decline do not suggest that it is any more than a correction," broker GNI said.
"Effectively the market seems to have done all that it needs to until it has further confirmation or negation of the recent bullish Ivorian crop forecast," it said in a commentary.
Others said both London and New York were also seen building a base before attempting a new rally.
Manufacturers have been forced to pay up to cover their short positions. This is helping the current rally, which is also fuelled by specs and fund buying.
In another story, Barry Callebaut, the company created through a merger between cocoa firms Cacao Barry SA and Callebaut AG, has been approved by a Belgian appeals court.
Barry Callebaut is a unit of Zurich-based Klaus J Jacobs Holding.

The decision will mean that Barry Callebaut will sell a portion of the rights, and the production of Belgium-based Cacao Goemaere to Chocolaterie Jacques, it said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
